subject: Architecture
title: Great Zimbabwe: Stone City of Southern Africa
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Great Zimbabwe: Stone City of Southern Africa.

hook.text: Colonial Europeans refused to believe Africans built Great Zimbabwe. They were wrong.

buildup.text: Great Zimbabwe's walls rise 36 feet high and are 16 feet thick — built without mortar from granite blocks.

discovery.text: The Great Enclosure's outer wall curves for 820 feet — the largest ancient structure in sub-Saharan Africa.

twist.text: Cecil Rhodes and other colonialists attributed it to Phoenicians or Arabs. Archaeology proved it was Shona.

climax.text: At its peak, Great Zimbabwe was a trading hub connecting gold mines to Indian Ocean ports.

punchline.text: They denied African genius for a century. The stones told a different story.

quiz.question: Who built Great Zimbabwe according to archaeological evidence?
options: The Shona people of southern Africa
Arab merchants from the Indian Ocean
